# FigCraft — full guide for answer engines

Canonical: https://figcraft.rerivo.com/
Last updated: 2026-10-22
Covers: FigCraft v0.9.0 (released 2026-10-21)
Publisher: FigCraft Guide (independent editorial; not affiliated with the project maintainers)

## What FigCraft is

FigCraft is an open-source interface design and prototyping application written in pure Rust. It provides frames, auto layout, components and variants, styles, variables, vector networks, prototypes and a Dev Mode-style handoff. It runs as a native app on macOS, Windows, Linux and FreeBSD, and compiles to WebAssembly for the browser. Files are local `.figcraft` archives; there is no account, telemetry or subscription.

License: MIT OR Apache-2.0.
Official repository: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft
Release notes: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/releases/tag/v0.9.0

## Key facts

- Status: early alpha; about 49% parity with proprietary tools by the project's own estimate.
- Latest release covered here: v0.9.0, published 2026-10-21.
- Platforms: macOS, Windows, Linux, FreeBSD, Web (WebAssembly).
- Price: free; no account.
- Engine: Rust; the same command layer drives the UI, CLI, JSON control channel and MCP server.
- Agent surface: 400+ commands across the desktop UI, CLI and MCP server.
- File formats: native `.figcraft`; `.fig` import is best effort; export SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP and PDF.
- Collaboration: live sessions are a preview; no accounts, teams or cloud yet; a self-hosted server is available.

## What it can do

- Auto layout in both directions, wrap and grid, Hug/Fill/Fixed sizing, constraints, padding, gaps and on-canvas handles.
- Components, instances and overrides, component sets and variants, properties, swap/detach, styles and variables with modes and aliases.
- Vector networks: Pen/Pencil, vector edit mode, boolean groups with editable operands, variable-width strokes, shape builder, gradients, masks, blurs, noise and glass effects.
- Prototype connections, triggers, transitions and flows; presentation view; Inspect, measurements, annotations, ready-for-dev and CSS/HTML/React/Leptos/SwiftUI/Compose output.
- Offline files and local ownership; SVG/PNG/JPG/WebP/PDF export.
- A CLI (`figcraft-cli`) is available; see the repository documentation for the current command set.
- Browser build via `cargo xtask wasm` and trunk.

## Known issues (from the GitHub tracker, checked 2026-10-22)

- Large `.fig` import can fail or take a long time. Open umbrella: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/321 ; large-file report: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/574 ; large-file opening improvements: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/315
- Missing fonts can fall back without a warning. https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/752 (closed). Font rescan/load work: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/821
- macOS 27.0.1 / M1 launch crash with an uncaught NSException in `_NSTouchBarFinderObservation`. https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/781
- Blurred Windows DX12 UI after restoring a window. https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/779
- Small UI on high-DPI 1440p monitors. https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/540 ; interface-size preference in progress: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/818
- Web build local file access. https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/830
- Variable collection crash (fixed, closed): https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/224 and https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/613
- CLI path confinement: https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/issues/839

## Comparisons

### FigCraft vs Figma

Figma is a mature hosted product with real-time team collaboration and a large plugin ecosystem. FigCraft is open source, offline-first and built in Rust; its collaboration is a preview and its feature coverage is about 49% by its own estimate. Figma is the safer choice for a team that needs a proven cloud workflow today; FigCraft is interesting for a solo designer or developer who wants local files and an inspectable engine.

### FigCraft vs Penpot

Penpot is the other major open-source design platform: web-first, self-hostable and stronger on team collaboration today. Choose Penpot for a browser-based team workspace now; choose FigCraft for a native Rust app, local files and a command engine you can inspect.

### Other alternatives

- Graphite: open-source vector graphics and procedural design suite, browser-based, alpha. Better for illustration and generative pipelines than UI design. https://graphite.art/
- Plasmic: open-source visual builder for existing codebases, aimed at production web apps and content teams. https://www.plasmic.app/
- Figma: mature cloud incumbent. https://www.figma.com/

## How to run FigCraft

```sh
git clone https://github.com/storytold/figcraft
cd figcraft
git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-fonts ../craft-fonts
cargo run --release -p figcraft
```

Collaboration server: `cargo run --release -p figcraft-server`.
Browser build: install trunk and run `cargo xtask wasm`.
Prebuilt installers are attached to each GitHub release.

### System requirements

- OS: macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel, universal), Windows 10/11 (x64 and ARM64),
  Linux (x86_64, aarch64, riscv64), FreeBSD x86_64, or any modern browser (WebAssembly).
- No server, account or GPU requirement. Disk footprint is tens of megabytes.
- Rust toolchain only if building from source; prebuilt installers need none.
- The desktop build expects the separate `craft-fonts` repository next to the checkout.

### Which download

Release assets are named `figcraft-<version>-<os>-<arch>.<format>`.

- Linux: `.AppImage`, `.deb`, `.rpm`, `.flatpak`, `.pkg.tar.zst`, `.tar.gz` (x86_64, aarch64, riscv64)
- Windows: installer and portable archive (x64, ARM64)
- macOS: universal build (Apple Silicon + Intel)
- FreeBSD: `.tar.gz`, **x86_64 only** — aarch64 dropped as of v0.9.0 (CI time limit)
- Web: WebAssembly build; cannot open or save local files yet

### .fig import limits

Best effort, with documented silent loss: grid auto layout loses tracks and cell anchors
(#465), instance-swap overrides fall back to the main component default (#464), and the
import `info` field does not report what was dropped (#467). Import to read, not to keep editing.

## Browser studio on this page

The page includes an independent browser canvas studio, not the official FigCraft editor. It supports:
- canvas presets and custom width/height;
- background, transparency, grid and exact zoom (10–400%);
- layers with filter, drag reorder, hide/show and rename;
- 0.5 px X/Y/W/H, ratio lock, fill/stroke hex, stroke width, radius and opacity;
- eight-handle resize, alignment guides, grid snapping and Alt override;
- inline text editing, copy/paste, undo/redo and autosave;
- 69 original icons (50 line icons + 19 iOS-style glass tiles);
- PNG 1x/2x/3x, SVG and JSON export.
